source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
To preserve quality and get a high market price, jackfruit should be harvested when the fruit has developed a ripe, fragrant smell, which also makes it easier to handle and transport to distant markets. Fruit should not be left on the tree to over-ripen, because it becomes vulnerable to damage from animals/pests and spoils easily.

The fruit stem should be cut with a knife. Freshly cut fruit should be handled carefully and kept away from letting it fall directly onto the ground, which would bruise or split it. The illustration shows two harvesters cutting jackfruit from a tree with a knife and collecting the fruit into baskets set on the ground.
